'''Maureen Ann Donnelly''' (born 1954) is an American [[herpetologist]] based at [[Florida International University]]. 

==Education and career==
She received her B.A. degree from [[California State University, Fullerton]] in 1977<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Curriculum vitae of maureen a. donnelly - Department of Biological ... |url=https://www.yumpu.com/en/document/read/5346752/curriculum-vitae-of-maureen-a-donnelly-department-of-biological- |access-date=2022-06-28 |website=yumpu.com |language=en}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=June 2022}} and graduated from the [[University of Miami]] with her doctorate degree in 1987.<ref name="Beolens Watkins Grayson 2011 p. 247">{{cite book|vauthors=Beolens B, Watkins M, Grayson M |title=The Eponym Dictionary of Reptiles|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|location=Baltimore, Maryland|year=2011|isbn=978-1-4214-0227-7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0F758vNQ0UUC&pg=PT247 | accessdate=May 26, 2016|page=247}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Territoriality in the poison-dart frog Dendrobates pumilio (Anura: Dendrobatidae). |date=1987 |language=English |first=Maureen A |last=Donnelly |oclc=612736059}}</ref> Following her Ph.D., she held postdoctoral positions at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] and the University of Miami. She joined the faculty of Florida International University in 1994 and, as of 2022, is a professor in the biological sciences department.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-31 |title=People |url=https://herpetologylab.org/people/ |access-date=2022-06-28 |website=FIU HERPETOLOGY |language=en}}</ref>

Donnelly served as president of the [[American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society Documents {{!}} American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists |url=https://asih.org/about/society-documents |access-date=2020-03-09 |website=asih.org}}</ref>

==Research==
Donnelly's research focuses on the ecology, behavior, and conservation of tropical amphibians and reptiles. Donnelly's early research was on the use of space in the early development of tadpoles.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Donnelly |first=Maureen A. |date=1989 |title=Effects of reproductive resource supplementation on space-use patterns in Dendrobates pumilio |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00379808 |journal=Oecologia |language=en |volume=81 |issue=2 |pages=212–218 |doi=10.1007/BF00379808 |pmid=28312540 |bibcode=1989Oecol..81..212D |s2cid=11726914 |issn=0029-8549|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Donnelly |first=Maureen A. |date=1989 |title=Demographic Effects of Reproductive Resource Supplementation in a Territorial Frog, Dendrobates Pumilio |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2307/1942599 |journal=Ecological Monographs |language=en |volume=59 |issue=3 |pages=207–221 |doi=10.2307/1942599 |jstor=1942599 |bibcode=1989EcoM...59..207D |issn=0012-9615|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

She has examined the loss of amphibians and reptiles, using Costa Rica as a model for global issues with biodiversity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Whitfield |first1=Steven M. |last2=Bell |first2=Kristen E. |last3=Philippi |first3=Thomas |last4=Sasa |first4=Mahmood |last5=Bolaños |first5=Federico |last6=Chaves |first6=Gerardo |last7=Savage |first7=Jay M. |last8=Donnelly |first8=Maureen A. |date=2007-05-15 |title=Amphibian and reptile declines over 35 years at La Selva, Costa Rica |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=104 |issue=20 |pages=8352–8356 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0611256104 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=1895953 |pmid=17449638|doi-access=free |bibcode=2007PNAS..104.8352W }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 2017 Donnelly received the Robert K. Johnson Award for Excellence in Service from the American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2018 |title=Award Announcements |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/26872503 |journal=Copeia |volume=106 |issue=1 |pages=1–9 |doi=10.1643/OT-18-008 |jstor=26872503 |s2cid=198153050 |issn=0045-8511|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
